facts.fact: 她心情极差：认识的人要么消失、要么死、要么又死又消失；她在街上想问同龄母亲——你认识的人也在集体死吗？难道大家该像没事一样？还是大多数人根本不认识同性恋和瘾君子？
facts.anchor: I was in a lousy mood. I kept thinking, Everyone I know can’t just disappear, or die, or die and disappear. Wasn’t anyone else losing it? I walked down the street and I’d see a woman my age with her kids and I’d want to ask her, Excuse me, is everyone you know dying too? But were the rest of us supposed to go along like everything was normal? Or did most people simply not know any homos and junkies? What kind of a life would that be?

facts.fact: Cynthia 母亲（楼上）的公寓空了——不只是清空过，而是那种「无人曾在此、也无人会再来」的空。
facts.anchor: It was empty. And I don’t mean the space had been cleared out, though it had been.

facts.fact: 通常下城拥挤得像装满账单车票的皮夹、连炮台公园的能量都稠到像要把岛尖压沉；这间房却空白得像一张复印纸。
facts.anchor: But this room just felt blank as a sheet of copy paper. It felt like no one had ever been there, and no one would ever come in.

facts.fact: 令她反感的是那种「什么都没有」——连死者都没有；下楼时她意识到自己不知道那位老太太的名字。（她还想起这像 François 被带走后的自家公寓，也像那间冷冻库。）
facts.anchor: It was the nothing that was so offensive, this lack of anything living or dead. On my way down the stairs, I realized I didn’t know the old woman’s name.

facts.fact: 她对 Cynthia 暗示对方做的勾当；Cynthia 只答：我没法跟那种负能量共处——闭眼打了个寒颤。
facts.anchor: I can’t live with that kind of negativity.” She shut her eyes, shuddered.

facts.fact: 孩子们问 Silverman 是否杀了老太太；她对孩子们说：她已经死了——他只是把她的鬼锁进那个盒子。
facts.anchor: “She was dead already,” I said. “He just locked her ghost up in that box.”

facts.fact: 她炸了：「如此这般（as such）？少拿 as such 跟我扯。你到底信不信有鬼？」
facts.anchor: As such? Fuck outta here with ‘as such.’ Do you even believe in ghosts?”

facts.fact: Silverman：我信，但我是科学家，我检验自己的信念；经验所得是——并不是每个人都留下什么，而当他们留下时，多半让生者难以承受。
facts.anchor: I do, yes. But I’m also a scientist. I test my beliefs. And what I have learned, empirically, is that not everyone leaves something of themselves behind. And when they do, more often than not, what’s left behind is difficult for the living to bear.”

facts.fact: 她的立场：那就怕一点吧！带着那种感觉活一分钟，又不是世界末日。
facts.anchor: So be a little scared! Live with that feeling for a minute, it’s not the end of the world.”

facts.fact: 他的辩解：帮助人们把东西收起来，是慈悲。
facts.anchor: I think it’s compassionate to help people put things away.

facts.fact: 他的家史：母亲乘 Kindertransport 来，父亲年长；战后在海法相识、父亲考上医学院后迁居纽约；他生于此地。
facts.anchor: My mother was on the Kindertransport. My father was older.” He spoke slowly, as if leaving space for the gaps in his story. “They met in Haifa after the war. They moved to New York when my father got into medical school. I was born here.

facts.fact: 他说父母试图保护他免受他们经历的一切——但那些东西他们自己也没能留下。
facts.anchor: They tried to protect me from everything they experienced. But they couldn’t leave it behind.”

facts.fact: 她的回应（用他偏好的措辞）：对灵在敏感的人对它们负有责任——不只是为它们，因为拒看别人的痛苦，就等于否认自己身上的同一份痛。
facts.anchor: I think that people who are sensitive to presences have a responsibility to them,” I said, as patiently as I could, using the words he preferred, like I was talking to that little kid he once was. “Not just for them. But because refusing to look at the pain of others is denying that same pain in yourself.”

facts.fact: Silverman（此时她读不出其表情）：你有能力，它不该是你的负担。
facts.anchor: “You have an ability,” he said. “It shouldn’t be a burden to you.”

facts.fact: 他的招募：你可以帮我们。（她张嘴，无话可说，又闭上。他还说她老板要卖楼。）
